sliding-window__longest-substring-withou.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
sliding-window__longest-substring-withou.statement: Given a string `s`, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeating characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces

approaches.name: Window with last-seen map
approaches.idea: Keep `left` at the start of the current valid window. For each `right`, if the current char was last seen at an index `>= left`, jump `left` to `seen[c] + 1` (never move it backward). Record the max width as you go.

sliding-window__longest-substring-withou.insight: Store the last index of each char and jump `left` forward (guard with `last[c] >= left` so it never moves backward). No per-step inner loop needed.

sliding-window__minimum-window-substring.title: Minimum Window Substring
sliding-window__minimum-window-substring.statement: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the smallest substring of `s` that contains all characters of `t` (including multiplicity). Return `""` if no such window exists.

examples.explanation: `BANC` is the minimal window containing A, B and C.

constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Expand then contract with a formed counter
approaches.idea: `need[c]` holds required counts and `required` the distinct chars needed. Expand `right`; when a char's window count reaches its required count, increment `formed`. While `formed == required`, record the best window and contract `left`, decrementing `formed` on the `== need[c]` transition.

sliding-window__minimum-window-substring.insight: Track a single `formed` counter (how many distinct chars are fully satisfied) instead of re-scanning the map; the `== need[c]` transition is what moves `formed` up and down.

sliding-window__subarrays-with-k-differe.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
sliding-window__subarrays-with-k-differe.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the number of contiguous subarrays that contain exactly `k` distinct integers.

approaches.name: Difference of atMost windows
approaches.idea: Counting subarrays with exactly `k` distinct directly is awkward, but subarrays with at most `k` distinct is a clean sliding window: for each `right`, `right - left + 1` new subarrays end at `right`. Exactly `k` = atMost(k) - atMost(k-1).

sliding-window__subarrays-with-k-differe.insight: When "exactly K" resists a direct window, compute atMost(K) - atMost(K-1); atMost adds `right - left + 1` per step.

sliding-window__sliding-window-maximum.title: Sliding Window Maximum
sliding-window__sliding-window-maximum.statement: Given an array `nums` and a window size `k`, return an array of the maximum value in each contiguous window of size `k` as it slides from left to right.

approaches.name: Monotonic deque
approaches.idea: Maintain a deque of indices whose values are strictly decreasing front-to-back. Before appending `i`, pop smaller values from the back (they can never be a future max while `nums[i]` is in range) and drop the front if it falls out of the window. The front is always the current window's max.

sliding-window__sliding-window-maximum.insight: Store indices, not values, in a decreasing deque: pop the back while it is <= the incoming value, evict the front when it leaves the window, and the front is the max.

sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct
sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.statement: Given a string `s` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest substring of `s` that contains at most `k` distinct characters.

approaches.name: Window with a count map
approaches.idea: Expand `right`, adding each char to a frequency map. Whenever the map holds more than `k` distinct keys, shrink from `left`, removing keys whose count hits zero. The window is always valid after shrinking, so track its max width.

sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.insight: `map.size()` is the live distinct count; shrink only while it exceeds `k` and remove a key exactly when its count drops to zero.

sliding-window__substring-with-concatena.title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
sliding-window__substring-with-concatena.statement: Given a string `s` and an array `words` of equal-length strings, return all starting indices of substrings in `s` that are a concatenation of every word in `words` exactly once, in any order, with no characters in between.

examples.explanation: `barfoo` at 0 and `foobar` at 9 are concatenations of the two words.

constraints: s and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Sliding window per word-length offset
approaches.idea: All words share length `wl`, so any valid match aligns to one of `wl` offsets. For each offset run a word-level sliding window: step `wl` at a time, count matched words, shrink when a word's count exceeds its need or when a full match (`count == n`) is found, and skip forward past any word not in the dictionary.
approaches.time: O(wl * (n / wl)) = O(n) word steps, each O(wl) for substring
approaches.space: O(m * wl) for the word maps (m = words.length)

sliding-window__substring-with-concatena.insight: Because every word is the same length, only `wl` alignments matter; run a word-granularity sliding window on each offset instead of re-checking every index.

sliding-window__minimum-number-of-k-cons.title: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
sliding-window__minimum-number-of-k-cons.pattern: Greedy left-to-right + difference array of flip effects
sliding-window__minimum-number-of-k-cons.statement: Given a binary array `nums` and an integer `k`, in one move you flip a contiguous subarray of exactly `k` bits (0->1, 1->0). Return the minimum number of moves to make the whole array all 1s, or -1 if impossible.

approaches.name: Greedy with running flip parity
approaches.idea: Scan left to right keeping `current` = number of active flips covering position `i` (via a difference array). The effective value is `nums[i] ^ (current & 1)`; if it is 0 the leftmost fix must start here, so flip `[i, i+k-1]`. If that window runs off the end, return -1. Each 0 forces at most one flip, so greedy is optimal.

sliding-window__minimum-number-of-k-cons.insight: Track flip effects with a difference array so `current`'s parity tells you the live bit value in O(1); the leftmost 0 forces its own window, so greedy is optimal.

sliding-window__count-number-of-nice-sub.title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
sliding-window__count-number-of-nice-sub.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, a subarray is nice if it contains exactly `k` odd numbers. Return the number of nice subarrays.

examples.explanation: [1,1,2,1] and [1,2,1,1] each hold exactly 3 odd numbers.
16 subarrays contain exactly two odd numbers.

approaches.name: Difference of atMost windows
approaches.idea: Treat odd numbers as 1 and even as 0. Subarrays with at most `k` odds is a clean sliding window that adds `right - left + 1` per step. Exactly `k` odds = atMost(k) - atMost(k-1).

sliding-window__count-number-of-nice-sub.insight: Map odd->1, even->0 and reuse the atMost(K) - atMost(K-1) trick; the parity `& 1` is the only per-element work.

sliding-window__replace-the-substring-fo.title: Replace the Substring for Balanced String
sliding-window__replace-the-substring-fo.pattern: Minimize window whose complement is feasible
sliding-window__replace-the-substring-fo.statement: You are given a string `s` of length `n` (a multiple of 4) containing only the characters 'Q','W','E','R'. The string is balanced when each character appears exactly `n/4` times. Return the minimum length of a substring you can replace (with any of these characters) to make `s` balanced.

examples.explanation: Replace one 'Q' with 'R' to get a balanced string.

constraints: 4 <= n <= 10^5, n is a multiple of 4

approaches.name: Shrink the replaceable window
approaches.idea: Whatever lies inside the replaced window can be rewritten freely, so a window is valid iff every character's count OUTSIDE it is <= n/4. Keep counts of the outside region: as `right` advances, remove `s[right]` from the outside; while the outside is balanced, record the window length and add `s[left]` back as `left` advances. Minimize the window length.

sliding-window__replace-the-substring-fo.insight: The window is what you replace, so validity depends on the counts OUTSIDE it being <= n/4; keep the outside counts and shrink while the outside stays feasible.

sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.title: Longest Substring with At Least K Repeating Characters
sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.pattern: Window constrained by target unique count / divide & conquer
sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.statement: Given a string `s` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest substring in which every character appears at least `k` times.
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Sliding window bounded by unique-char target
approaches.idea: A plain expanding window has no monotonic validity here, so fix the number of distinct characters `unique` from 1..26 and run a window that keeps exactly `unique` distinct chars. Track how many of them already appear >= k times; when the count of distinct equals `unique` and all of them meet the threshold, the window is valid.

approaches.name: Divide and conquer on rare characters
approaches.idea: Any character appearing fewer than `k` times can never be inside the answer, so it becomes a split point. Recurse on the pieces between such characters; if none exist in a segment, the whole segment is valid.

sliding-window__longest-substring-with-a.insight: Validity is not monotonic for a single window, so either fix the distinct-char count (1..26) to restore monotonicity, or split on characters that occur fewer than k times.
